items.followUp: How do homologous chromosomes orient at the equator during metaphase I?

rubric.why: This identifies the chromosome pairs and their position in metaphase I.
rubric.description: Homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) line up at the equatorial plane.
rubric.how: Award for stating that homologous pairs or bivalents arrange at the equator.

rubric.why: This describes the spindle attachment that helps form the metaphase arrangement.
rubric.description: Spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.
rubric.how: Award for stating that spindle fibres attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.

modelAnswer: Homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) arrange themselves along the equatorial plane, forming the metaphase plate.
Spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the chromosomes at their centromeres.

items.followUp: Name the main products of glycolysis and state its net ATP yield.

rubric.why: This identifies the main carbon-containing product and its quantity.
rubric.description: Glycolysis produces two molecules of pyruvate (pyruvic acid).
rubric.how: Award for naming two pyruvate or two pyruvic acid molecules.

rubric.why: This identifies the net ATP yield from glycolysis.
rubric.description: Glycolysis yields a net two ATP molecules; it also produces two NADH molecules.
rubric.how: Award for stating that glycolysis yields two ATP (or a net yield of two ATP).

modelAnswer: One glucose molecule produces two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate) in glycolysis.
The net yield is two ATP molecules; two NADH molecules are also produced.
